us.label: US News
us.subtitle: Top domestic stories from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump bid to restrict mail ballots before midterms
bullets: The Supreme Court rejected the administration’s emergency push to change mail-ballot rules with voting already underway.
States can continue using existing mail-ballot procedures for the 2026 midterm elections.
Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas publicly dissented from the order.

articles.title: Fed expected to raise rates despite Trump’s calls for cuts
bullets: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to lift its benchmark rate Wednesday for the first time in three years.
AP reported the move would be aimed at stubborn inflation and would defy Trump’s demands for lower rates.
Futures markets were pricing in possible additional hikes in December and March.

articles.title: US confirms for first time that it has deployed weapons in space
bullets: Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said the US has fielded on-orbit space-control weapons.
He did not disclose what the weapons are or how they operate.
The confirmation comes amid longstanding US concern over Russian and Chinese space threats.

articles.title: EPA eliminates Biden-era greenhouse-gas limits on power plants
bullets: The EPA said it is repealing rules limiting climate pollution from coal- and gas-fired power plants.
The agency also announced a related step aimed at blocking future climate-focused power-plant regulations.
Environmental groups criticized the rollback, while EPA said it would save industry costs and support energy production.

articles.title: DHS voter probe may violate state laws, whistleblower alleges
bullets: A federal whistleblower alleged DHS employees were told to misrepresent themselves on voter lookup tools.
The report said the initiative could wrongly implicate US citizens using unreliable data.
DHS said it is focused on prosecuting and removing noncitizens who vote.

global.label: Global
global.subtitle: Major worldwide developments from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: NATO fighter jet shoots down drone over Lithuania
bullets: A NATO fighter shot down a drone that entered Lithuanian airspace shortly after midnight Tuesday.
Lithuanian officials said the drone likely entered from Belarus and was downed near Pratkunai village.
The incident raised concern about the Ukraine war spilling over NATO borders.

articles.title: Ukraine races to counter Russia’s jet-powered drone attacks
bullets: Ukraine is testing new interceptor systems against Russia’s jet-powered attack drones.
Reuters reported the military brought producers together in July to test the next generation of defenses.
The effort follows months of damaging Russian drone strikes against Ukrainian targets.

articles.title: Hungary government moves to roll back Orban-era anti-LGBTQ+ rules
bullets: Hungary’s government submitted a bill to remove rules restricting LGBTQ+ content for under-18s.
The rules were introduced under Viktor Orban’s former nationalist government.
Reuters reported the move follows EU legal pressure over the restrictions.

articles.title: North Korea’s Kim vows to deepen ties with Russia
bullets: Kim Jong Un said North Korea would expand and deepen joint work with Russia.
The message to Vladimir Putin was reported by state media KCNA on Tuesday.
Kim also backed Russia’s victory in what he called a sacred war.

articles.title: Houthis strike Saudi Arabia as Gulf-Iran talks are postponed
bullets: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis launched a new attack on Saudi Arabia on Monday.
Gulf Arab states postponed planned talks with Iran amid the escalation.
The developments heightened concerns about wider Middle East conflict and oil-supply risks.

india.label: India News
india.subtitle: Top India stories from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: J&K High Court quashes detention of man labelled Lashkar overground worker
bullets: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court quashed a Public Safety Act order against Ishfaq Ahmad Wani.
The court said preventive detention cannot rest on mere labels without specific factual grounds.
It noted Wani had already been granted bail in the case cited by authorities.

articles.title: Bihar opens 211 colleges and plans overseas training for teachers
bullets: Bihar opened 211 new degree colleges in a single day, according to state officials.
The higher education department plans to select 100 professors for training at Oxford and other institutions.
Officials said the new colleges target block towns that previously lacked degree colleges.

articles.title: Madhya Pradesh probes alleged moong procurement fraud
bullets: Farmers in Raisen district allegedly found moong sales recorded in their names despite not growing or selling the crop.
The Economic Offences Wing booked three computer operators tied to procurement terminals.
Investigators allege fake registrations were used to sell market-bought moong to the government at MSP rates.

articles.title: India and Vietnam agree to deepen defence ties and co-produce equipment
bullets: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met Vietnamese Foreign Minister Le Hoai Trung in New Delhi.
The two sides agreed to deepen defence and security cooperation, including co-production of Indian defence items.
They also discussed trade, supply chains, connectivity, nuclear energy and space cooperation.

articles.title: Indian Railways announces more than 100 festival special trains
bullets: Indian Railways announced special trains for Durga Puja, Diwali, Chhath and other festive travel.
The routes connect states including Bihar, West Bengal, Assam, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
IRCTC said it has upgraded booking systems and added anti-bot technology for the festive period.

stocks.label: US Stocks
stocks.subtitle: Top US market movers from the latest session

articles.title: Nvidia drops as AI-slowdown fears hit chipmakers
bullets: Reuters reported Nvidia shares fell about 3.4% on Monday.
The decline came after AI leaders raised safety concerns and called for slowing model development.
The broader Philadelphia chip index also fell sharply during the session.

articles.title: Micron slides more than 5% in semiconductor rout
bullets: Micron Technology dropped more than 5% in Monday trading, according to Reuters.
Memory and chip names bore the brunt of selling tied to AI-investment concerns.
The decline came as Treasury yields and oil prices also pressured equities.

articles.title: Broadcom falls over 4% as AI-chip trade weakens
bullets: Broadcom shares fell more than 4% during Monday’s selloff.
Reuters linked the move to concerns that AI development and spending could slow.
The company was among several AI-linked semiconductor names under pressure.

articles.title: AMD drops more than 4% as chip stocks sell off
bullets: Advanced Micro Devices fell more than 4% on Monday, Reuters reported.
The selloff followed weekend calls by top AI executives for slower frontier-model development.
Semiconductor losses weighed on the Nasdaq and S&P 500.

articles.title: Microsoft gains while chip stocks fall
bullets: Microsoft rose 1.97% to $505.41 at Monday’s close, according to Reuters-linked Schwab data.
Reuters reported software stocks rallied even as chipmakers sold off.
The move reflected rotation toward software names seen as less exposed to a direct AI-capex slowdown.

business.label: Business
business.subtitle: Corporate and economic stories from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: Baldwin Group to go private in $7.7 billion deal
bullets: Reuters’ Wall Street Journal digest reported Dell-linked DFO Management and Sequence Holdings will take Baldwin Group private.
The deal values the insurance broker at $7.7 billion.
The report said the move is intended to give Baldwin more flexibility to pursue AI investments.

articles.title: Accenture to pay $25 million over US diversity-practices allegations
bullets: Reuters’ WSJ digest reported Accenture will pay $25 million to settle US government allegations.
The allegations concerned diversity practices targeted by the Trump administration.
The digest said Reuters had not independently verified the Wall Street Journal report.

articles.title: OpenAI buys smartphone-camera startup Glass Imaging
bullets: Reuters’ WSJ digest reported OpenAI acquired Glass Imaging.
The startup develops higher-quality camera technology for smartphones.
The transaction valued Glass Imaging at more than $300 million, according to the digest.

articles.title: Senate to vote on major crypto regulation bill amid Trump ethics fight
bullets: The Senate is set to vote Tuesday on whether to advance a new cryptocurrency regulatory framework.
AP described it as a pivotal test for the $2.3 trillion crypto market.
Democrats argue the bill does not go far enough to address Trump-linked crypto investments.

articles.title: Essar Energy Transition Retail acquires UK forecourt network SGN Retail
bullets: Essar Energy Transition Retail acquired the UK forecourt network SGN Retail.
The Indian Express reported the deal supports Essar’s strategy to integrate fuel production with fuel retailing in the UK.
The acquisition was reported on September 14.

tech.label: Tech
tech.subtitle: Technology developments from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: Microsoft commits to AI privacy rules for students
bullets: Microsoft agreed to sweeping AI safety and privacy standards for schools.
The rules say the burden of protecting student privacy should fall on tech companies, not families or schools.
The move comes as New York City and Los Angeles pause student AI use for one year.

articles.title: Gates Foundation pledges $1 billion to expand AI access
bullets: Bill Gates warned AI could deepen inequality if access is not broadened.
The Gates Foundation pledged $1 billion to improve AI access and use for social benefit.
AP reported Gates is urging world leaders and tech companies to act now.

articles.title: Tech CEOs call for AI regulation as Washington hesitates
bullets: AP reported that leading AI executives are warning more urgently about potential harms from AI.
The calls have met resistance from President Trump and slow movement in Congress.
House Democrats planned a private Tuesday discussion on AI, according to AP.

articles.title: China narrows AI gap with the United States
bullets: AP reported China is closing the technology gap with the US as global AI-risk debate intensifies.
Analysts described the gap between US and Chinese models as narrow and fragile.
The story highlights rising competition over frontier AI capabilities.

articles.title: Microsoft drafts code of conduct to keep its AI under human control
bullets: Microsoft unveiled a draft code of conduct for its in-house AI systems.
Reuters reported the code reflects growing concern that powerful AI must remain under human control.
The release followed calls by Anthropic and OpenAI leaders to pace AI development for safety.
